text:
jamie: Heads-up — ran a compare between streaming(push) and non-streaming(polling) on the replay harness this morning. weird results: streaming wins p50/p90 but p95 and throughput are worse for some kernels. also saw KV cache hit rate drop ~12%. anyone seen this pattern before?

alex: Interesting. did you keep the client readloop the same? push vs polling changes timing & backpressure a lot.

jamie: I ran push for streaming and polling for non-streaming (what the browser path does). I can re-run polling+streaming but wanted to check hypotheses first.

marta: two quick suspects: (1) chunking changes prefix distribution so KV lookups miss more often, (2) streaming readloop induces extra memcpy/copy paths -> kernel selection fallback. profiling showed more time in "stream_dispatch" when chunked.

diego: can you paste the bench flags you used? small differences in sequence-length sampling matter. also check warmup phase for KV cache.

jamie: here are the flags i used:
```
bench --mode=replay --streaming --chunk-size=256 --client=push --seq-dist=prod-sampled.json --warmup-requests=2000 --kernels=auto
bench --mode=replay --streaming=false --client=polling --seq-dist=prod-sampled.json --warmup-requests=2000 --kernels=auto
```

alex: ah, kernels=auto can flip to the small-seq kernel if it thinks effective sequence is short. with chunking the runtime might see many short segments and pick a different kernel which hurts throughput. pin kernel with `--kernels=prefer-long` for apples-to-apples.

marta: also: check KV hit accounting — the replay harness currently emits per-request kv_hit bool only for completed responses; streaming interleaves partial outputs so some hits are not attributed properly. I filed a small patch to emit kv probes on prefix decode boundaries.

ci-bot: perf/regression: streaming-readloop p95 increased by +18% on main. See: https://ci.internal/redwood/12345 (CI artifact attached) :warning:

diego: for KV hit rate i usually do this quick grep + aggregate on the runner logs:
```
cat runner.log | jq -r '.events[] | select(.type=="kv_probe") | .hit' | uniq -c
```
ran it on the failing run and got: 87% -> 75% between non-streaming -> streaming.

jamie: Nice. so hypothesis: streaming changes client interarrival + chunk boundaries -> more KV misses + runtime switches kernel -> net worse p95/throughput.

alex: Also watch the client readloop CPU pattern. polling tends to batch reads and reduce syscalls; push can cause many small read() syscalls. That plus backpressure stalling can make the readloop spin or thrash, increasing tail latency. We should measure syscall counters and per-thread CPU.

marta: action item: add a synthetic client that reproduces browser chunking (small variable-sized chunks with jitter) and run both push/polling with pinned kernel + identical seq-dist + explicit KV warmup. I'll sketch harness today.

diego: small perf tweak worth trying: reduce max_batch_size for streaming path to avoid head-of-line blocking on long requests. tradeoff might be throughput but can help p95. also try enabling `tcp_cork`/`TCP_NODELAY` variants in readloop perf test — network coalescing interacts with chunking.

jamie: Good. can we agree on an apples-to-apples checklist to run? I'll run and record results in bench-corpus under tag `streaming-vs-polling-2026-03-18`. Proposed checklist:
1) same client binary (we'll use synthetic-client v2)
2) identical seq-length distribution file
3) KV warmup requests = 2000 (and measure hit rate after warmup)
4) pin kernels during each run (`--kernels=prefer-long` or `--kernels=prefer-short`)
5) record per-thread cpu+syscall counters + kernel selection log
6) run both push & polling with chunk-size sweep [64,128,256,512] and jitter on chunk intervals
7) collect raw runner logs + perf map + kernel trace

alex: sounds good. i'll run a quick 30m sweep on espresso (no autoscale) tonight and post raw artifacts.

marta: i'll add the synthetic-client + kv-probe fix to a branch and open MR.

diego: i'll prepare a flamegraph job to run after alex finishes. also will add a small sample script to compute effective prefix-length distribution from the replay traces.

jamie: Perfect. tagging this thread `perf:streaming-bench`. i'll follow up with results and we'll decide on batching heuristic changes if needed. thanks all :rocket:
